brief.headline: Move to 30-day payment terms to free ₹44.91 L working capital — we pay on delivery while they stretch their own suppliers to 63d, and their below-peer 5.4% margin limits room for price cuts.

priceAsk.summary: Benchmark laminate film cost to import unit value; offer 6.7% early-pay discount if we compress lead-time or pay cash
priceAsk.target: 171.60 ₹/kg market line for BOPET film import unit value; or a 6.7% discount for accelerated cash
priceAsk.basis: Market benchmark for BOPET film is 171.60 ₹/kg; their effective borrowing cost is 6.7%, so faster payment saves them that rate and justifies a matching discount

paymentTermAsk.summary: Shift from Immediate payment to 30-day credit, freeing ₹44.91 L working capital for FDC

brief.financialLeverage: Tetrapak earns a 5.4% net margin, well below the 10.2% peer median, so deep price cuts will hurt them. Their 1.09x debt-to-equity ratio and 6.7% borrowing cost mean they value cash but carry leverage risk. They stretch their own suppliers to 63d payables versus a 6d peer median, and run a 75d cash cycle against 30d peers — they already play the working-capital game aggressively. We are 0.12% of their ₹4491.70 Cr revenue, so standalone volume leverage is negligible. Their C (59/100) health score, Altman Z of 2.15 (grey zone), and severe legal cases flag continuity risk. Push hard on payment terms where we have the worst deal in our portfolio (Immediate), but tread carefully on price — offer speed or volume in exchange, and qualify alternates to build competitive tension.

evidence.point: Their net margin is half the peer median
They stretch suppliers far longer than peers
Their cash conversion cycle runs 2.5× slower than peers
We pay them on delivery, the worst terms in our supplier base
Moving to 30-day credit frees nearly half a crore for FDC
We represent a tiny fraction of their business

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter, already a tiny FDC supplier, scalable second source for laminate sachets — revenue ₹2611.64 Cr, health C (59/100)

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant covering both film substrate and conversion, can second-source at scale — revenue ₹16492.00 Cr, health C (46/100)

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter specializing in pharma blister and sachet laminates, strong GEEP second-source — revenue ₹222.04 Cr, health D (31/100)

risks: Altman Z score of 2.15 sits in the grey distress zone — supply continuity is a watch; avoid a squeeze that tips a fragile supplier
Severe legal case(s) flagged in risk profile — verify operational stability and capacity before locking volume
22% goods-receipt reversal rate signals quality or documentation issues — address root cause before they cascade into line stoppages
At 0.12% of their revenue we lack standalone leverage — must bundle volume commitments, multi-year terms, or visible competitive alternate to move the needle
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to align our payment terms with industry norms — moving from immediate payment to 30 days will free ₹44.91 L working capital for us, and given you already run 63-day payables with your own suppliers, it's a fair shift.
